claims.text: An optimal Al content increases lattice distortion in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
An optimal Al content modifies local electron concentration and thereby stabilizes a metastable FCC matrix.
The metastable FCC matrix either remains intact during service or undergoes limited beneficial transformations.
Limited twinning or minor phase adjustment can sustain high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
A single-phase FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy can be formed at a near-optimal Al level.
Al0.3CoCrFeNi is an example of a composition near the proposed optimum.
Al induces chemical short-range ordering and local lattice distortions that modify defect interactions and phase-transformation thresholds.
Changing alloy chemistry can alter phase stability and associated strength–ductility behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Al-driven lattice distortion and valence-electron-concentration changes favor metastable FCC rather than deleterious phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni.
Retention of the FCC phase at high temperature ensures strength and environmental resistance.
The proposed metastable FCC alloy enables transformation-induced plasticity, including twinning, under cryogenic loading.
Al-induced structural features provide effective defect sinks under irradiation.
Relative to a sub-optimal-Al baseline, the optimal alloy will retain FCC with fewer unwanted secondary phases across cryogenic, high-temperature, irradiation, and environmental exposures.
The optimal alloy will have higher yield strength and better ductility retention at both cryogenic and high temperatures than the baseline.
The optimal alloy will accumulate fewer irradiation-induced defects than the baseline.
Both too little and too much Al destabilize FCC and can cause premature transformation to BCC or intermetallic phases with degraded performance.
The proposed mechanism is limited to a critical Al-content range near Al0.3 and to comparable thermomechanical histories that initially produce FCC.
Large composition or processing changes may activate different phase-stabilization mechanisms.

contradictions.description: Al0.3CoCrFeNi denotes an Al:Co:Cr:Fe:Ni molar ratio of 0.3:1:1:1:1, corresponding to about 7 at.% Al, whereas the boundary describes Al0.3 as approximately a mole fraction, which would imply about 30 at.% Al.
